title: Differentiable RL in Asset Allocation
basicDesc: A differentiable reinforcement learning approach for optimizing a policy.
desc: Through Pytorch's functions, the learning/trading environment can form a computational graph between the policy's trades and a loss metric. In this way, the policy can be trained to directly optimize for the metric using standard backpropagation instead of traditional reinforcement learning methods.
Train and validation loss converge slowly and require many epochs to realize improvements.
The Sequential Transform Layer
An interesting part of the policy's neural network, the STL(sequential transform layer), was inspired by GLMs(generalized linear models).
A standard GLM follows the form:
\[ y = \beta_0 + \sum_{i} \beta_i g(x_i) \]
where \(g\) is the link function that transforms \(x_i\).
Similarly, the STL is defined by:
\[ z = w_0 + \sum_{i}\sum_{j}w_{ij} g_j(\mathbf{x}_i) \]
where \( g_j: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n \) and \( \mathbf{x}_i \) is a feature of sequence length n.

The link function, in this case, \( g_j \), uses a dimension-preserving function selected from a set including: the identity function(no transform), discrete Fourier transform(with negative bins), rolling standard deviation, rolling maximum/minimum, velocity, acceleration, moving averages(with padding), etc., based on the index \( j \). All combinations between \( \mathbf{x}_i \) and \( g_j \) are weighed and summed.

With learnable weights, additivity, and layer stacking, the model can learn which transformations are most valuable inside the function set and create complex sequential features from nested transformations.
It is possible to use the complex values from the DFT to create a complex-valued network, but the current implementation separates the complex terms and converts it to a real values for simplicity.
Policy Architecture
The policy uses two encoders, one creating embeddings through 1D Convolution and the other with LSTMs.

To introduce exploration during training, the policy predicts a normal distribution of allocations(mu and log-sigma), where an allocation is randomly sampled. Using action sampling also appears to stabilize the policy's convergence.

Gated linear units applied on features, Kaiming weight initialization, and a custom loss metric borrowed from a Hull Tactical Kaggle competition greatly improved the policy's training stability and backtest performances.

title: Genetic Algorithms for Algorithmic Trading
basicDesc: A genetic algorithm system for evolving trading strategies using Python ASTs and Bayesian optimization.
desc: Using python abstract syntax trees to represent genes, algorithms can be randomly generated to process logic between technical indicators and output trading signals.

An individual consists of a minimum of one indicator gene, two logic genes, and one signal gene to interpret logic. Logic is arguably the most important gene and is able to compare two indicators(i2i), an indicator to the price(i2p), compare an indicator to a constant value(i2c), or compare one logic gene to another (l2l). Since logic genes can reference previously stated logic genes, they allow for complex logical compositions.

Indicator genes are the first genes generated, containing an indicator function and returning the available parameters for the bayesian optimizer to select. The logic gene can use one or two indicator/logic genes to create logical structures. The signal gene then selects one logic gene to use as the long signal and one as the sell/short signal, finally creating a basic algorithm.

The current implementation uses the following in order: population generation, bayesian optimization(via optuna), and staged pruning to find the best performing algorithm within a generated population.

title: BirdCLEF 2026
basicDesc: A bird sound classification model using EfficientNet-b0 with attention pooling and GLU layers.
desc: Starting from a Mel-scaled spectrogram, the efficientnet-b0 Convolutional Neural Network(with pretrained weights for faster convergence) is used as the model backbone to generate convoluted embeddings.
To efficiently reduce embedding dimensions, multi-scale adaptive average pooling combined with attention pooling give the main classifier network a widened perspective on the bird sounds.

In intermediary steps(between embedding and classification), GLUs(gated linear units) are used to create a "focusing" effect, allowing the network to learn which features to prioritize without using expensive self-attention.
It is crucial that the GLU weights are initialized close to 1, otherwise the randomly generated weights may interfere with learning.
Although performing below distilled Perch-based models, combining this architecture with time+frequency masking and temperature scaling gave a final score of 0.79241!

title: Jupiter-Based Live Trading System
basicDesc: A live trading system using Jupiter DEX API with asynchronous market data streaming and paper trading.
desc: Through the Jupiter Decentralized Exchange API, this system takes in an algorithm(any python function) and asynchronously feeds market data to it.
Market data is streamed from sources such as binance, and trades made by the algorithm are processed through the Jupiter Aggregator.
Features a live paper trading mode for forward testing. Latency and small price mismatches(between data source and DEX) are expected.
